blocks.content: Alongside stable network identity, the other pillar of StatefulSets is volumeClaimTemplates, ensuring each replica gets its own dedicated persistent volume, and reliably reconnects to that exact same volume across every recreation.

As introduced in the Storage module, volumeClaimTemplates in a StatefulSet spec automatically generates a distinct PVC for every replica, you do not have to hand-create a separate PVC for each one yourself.

blocks.alt: A PVC generated automatically for every single replica

blocks.content:
volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 10Gi

code.content:

  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 10Gi

codes.yaml:
volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 10Gi

blocks.content: Each generated PVC is genuinely dedicated to one specific replica, app-0 gets pvc-app-0, app-1 gets pvc-app-1, exactly the per-replica storage the previous module's Stateful Storage Concepts topic said this workload type needed.

blocks.alt: Individually dedicated storage, not one shared pool between replicas

blocks.content: 3. Reconnecting to the Exact Same Volume
blocks.text: 3. Reconnecting to the Exact Same Volume

blocks.content: This is the genuinely powerful part: when app-0 is recreated, whether from a crash or a node failure, it reconnects to its own original PVC, not a fresh, empty one, and never one belonging to a different replica.

blocks.alt: Always the same original volume back, never a random or different one

blocks.content: 4. Combined With Network Identity: the Same Logical Instance
blocks.text: 4. Combined With Network Identity: the Same Logical Instance

blocks.content: Put together with the stable DNS identity from the previous topic, this means a StatefulSet replica is, functionally, the same logical instance across any number of recreations, same name, same data, even though the underlying Pod object and its IP are technically new each time.

blocks.alt: Same name, same data, functionally the same instance every single time

blocks.content: 5. The Direct Contrast With Deployment Pods
blocks.text: 5. The Direct Contrast With Deployment Pods

blocks.content: An ordinary Deployment Pod, if it uses storage at all, has no particular attachment to any specific volume, any replica could, in principle, mount any available matching storage. A StatefulSet replica always reconnects to specifically its own, a genuinely different guarantee.

blocks.alt: No particular attachment versus a guaranteed, consistent reconnection every time

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: volumeClaimTemplates automatically generates a dedicated PVC per replica, and a recreated replica always reconnects to its own original volume, never a different one.
Combined with stable network identity, this makes a StatefulSet replica functionally the same logical instance across recreation, same name, same data, every time.
